title: Hom-colimit comparison at the third vertex
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let T be a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category] and let A and B be supplied essentially constant values of the denominator pro-diagrams at its first two vertices [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. There exist an object Y of D, a denominator s : Z′ -> T.obj₃ in S, and r : F(Z′) -> Y such that for every W in D the map Hom(Y,W) -> colim over (S/T.obj₃)^op of Hom(F(Z′′),W), sending phi to the class of r followed by phi at s, is bijective. No essentially constant cone at the third vertex is asserted.

proof.text: Extract the natural cones uX and uY and their retraction/common-stage witnesses from the supplied values A and B. Lemma 05SA gives lf : A -> B with uX(s) followed by F(f) equal to lf followed by uY(s′) for every denominator square.

Choose sY and its retraction rY. MS2 applied to T.mor1 and sY gives s1 and f1 with s1 followed by T.mor1 = f1 followed by sY. The common-stage clause for uX at s1 gives p : s -> sX and q : s -> s1 with F(q) = F(p) followed by rX followed by uX(s1). Set alpha = F(p) followed by rX and f = q followed by f1. Naturality of uX shows uX(s) followed by alpha is identity. The factorization equation followed by F(f1) and rY, the 05SA equation, and uY(sY) followed by rY = identity show F(f) followed by rY = alpha followed by lf. The arrows p and q need not belong to S; the object s already has a denominator in S. This avoids the extra equalization of the earlier plan.

Use TR1 to complete f to a distinguished triangle T′ and lf to a distinguished triangle U. MS6 completes the square (s,sY) to a triangle morphism d : T′ -> T with all components in S. Exactness of F and TR3 extend (alpha,rY) to a triangle morphism m : F(T′) -> U with third component gamma.

Use 05R9 to obtain the cofiltered category J of distinguished denominator triangles into T and its three initial vertex projections p1,p2,p3. Let H : J -> Triangle D be the diagram of F-image triangles and j0 the object d. For i=1,2 the map Hom(U_i,W) -> colim Hom(F(denominator_i),W) at p_i(j0), induced by m_i, is bijective: compose with the cone Hom-colimit bijection of 05PZ, and the retraction identity shows that this composite is the identity. Compose the comparison over J opposite with p_i opposite’s canonical final-colimit comparison; it is the preceding bijection. Since the canonical final-colimit comparison is injective, this proves the first two comparisons over J opposite bijective. This uses Mathlib Functor.bijective_colimitTypePrecomp and its representative formula directly, rather than restricting essentially constant cones.

Apply the general triangulated Hom-colimit comparison to H, U, j0 and m, using the first two comparisons just proved. It gives the bijective third comparison over J opposite. Compose with the canonical bijective colimit comparison for p3 opposite. Its representative formula sends [gamma followed by phi] at j0 to [gamma followed by phi] at p3(j0). Return U.obj3, that denominator, and gamma.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 05SC, LF clause; common-stage construction simplified by T1; direct Mathlib final-functor comparisons and the separate general five-term Hom comparison
